source_batch.unit_label: Module A: International Banking - Documentary Letters of Credit

facts.statement: The International Standard Banking Practice for the Examination of Documents under Documentary Credits (ISBP) is an ICC publication giving guidance on examining documents presented under credits. It cannot change UCP 600 but is a companion to it. It was first approved by the ICC in 2002 as a companion to UCP 500; after UCP 600 it was updated as ICC publication No. 681; a fully revised version, ICC publication No. 745, was published in July 2013 with new and reworded interpretations and additions from ICC official opinions. Its aims are uniformity of practice worldwide, to reduce the number of credits rejected for discrepancies, and practices that reduce discrepant presentations.

Incoterms are ICC rules for the interpretation of trade terms in contracts of sale, not contracts of carriage. Incoterms 2020 took effect on 1 January 2020 and has eleven rules: seven for any mode of transport (EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, DDP) and four for sea and inland waterway transport (FAS, FOB, CFR, CIF). DPU (Delivered at Place Unloaded) replaced DAT, and is the only rule under which the seller unloads the goods at destination.
facts.locator: Overview of Incoterms 2020; S03 printed p. 116 on contract of sale and the DPU change

facts.statement: Moving from EXW towards DDP the seller's obligations increase and the buyer's decrease: EXW puts the maximum responsibility on the buyer and DDP the maximum on the seller. In the courseware's matrix the seller bears warehouse services and export packing under every rule; loading at the port of origin and origin inland freight, port charges and forwarders' fees from FAS onward; ocean or air freight from CFR, CIF, CPT and CIP onward; destination port charges under DPU and DDP; and customs clearance and duties only under DDP.

The courseware lists these changes from Incoterms 2010 to 2020: under FCA the buyer can instruct its carrier to issue a bill of lading with an on-board notation to the seller so the seller can use it for bank financing; the rules allow the parties' own transport rather than a third party's (FCA, DAP, DPU, DDP); CIP by default requires cover under the Institute Cargo Clauses (A), all risks, rather than the limited cover of Clauses (C); DPU replaces DAT; costs are clearer in relation to carrier charges; and security obligations, such as mandatory screening of containers, are addressed.

Case-study principles in the courseware: a credit is separate from the sale or other contract, and banks deal in documents, not goods; a document may be dated before the date of the credit but not after the expiry date for presentation, unless the credit says otherwise; a presentation of more than one set of transport documents covering the same means of transport and the same journey is not a partial shipment even if the shipment dates differ; notice of refusal and discrepancy must be given by the close of the fifth banking day after the day of receipt of documents, and weekends and holidays are not banking days; insurance must be at least 110% of the invoice value if the credit is silent and must not be dated after the transport document unless it shows cover from the date of shipment; a bank that cannot advise a credit must inform the issuing bank at once, and the issuing bank is not responsible for the advising bank's failure; if the last day for presentation falls on a day the bank is closed, it extends to the next banking day.

payload.title: ISBP: the practice guide that sits beside UCP 600
payload.core_explanation_md:
**UCP 600** gives the rules. **ISBP** shows how bankers **apply** them when they check documents.

- It is an **ICC publication**, a **companion** to UCP 600.
- It **cannot change** UCP 600; it explains standard practice within it.
- **History**: approved in **2002** as a companion to UCP 500; updated as **ICC publication 681** after UCP 600 (2007); fully revised as **ICC publication 745** in **July 2013**, adding new interpretations and points drawn from ICC official opinions.
- **Aims**: **uniform practice worldwide**, **fewer credits rejected** for discrepancies, and practices that **reduce discrepant presentations**.

A note on currency: the ICC has since issued a later edition, **ISBP 821 (July 2023)**. The syllabus names **ISBP 745**, so this course teaches that edition and flags the newer one.

payload.title: Incoterms 2020: eleven rules in two families
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Incoterms** are ICC rules for the **contract of sale** (not the contract of carriage). They say who arranges and pays for carriage, insurance and customs, and **where risk passes**.

**Seven rules for any mode of transport**
- **EXW** Ex Works
- **FCA** Free Carrier
- **CPT** Carriage Paid To
- **CIP** Carriage and Insurance Paid To
- **DAP** Delivered at Place
- **DPU** Delivered at Place **Unloaded**
- **DDP** Delivered Duty Paid

**Four rules for sea and inland waterway only**
- **FAS** Free Alongside Ship
- **FOB** Free on Board
- **CFR** Cost and Freight
- **CIF** Cost, Insurance and Freight

In force since **1 January 2020**. **DPU replaced DAT**, and under DPU the seller **unloads** the goods at destination (under DAP the seller does not).

payload.title: Who carries what: the ladder from EXW to DDP
payload.core_explanation_md:
Read the rules as a ladder. **Each step towards DDP moves another job from buyer to seller.**

- **EXW**: the buyer takes almost everything, even **loading** the goods.
- **FAS, FCA, FOB**: the seller delivers to the **carrier or the ship**, so **loading at origin** and **origin charges** are the seller's.
- **CFR, CIF, CPT, CIP**: the seller also pays the **main carriage** (ocean or air freight). (CIF and CIP add **insurance**.)
- **DPU**: the seller also bears **destination port charges** and **unloads**.
- **DDP**: the seller also does **customs clearance and pays duties**, the maximum responsibility.

Wherever you are on the ladder, **warehouse services and export packing** are the seller's. **Customs clearance and duties** are the buyer's except under **DDP**.

payload.title: What changed between Incoterms 2010 and 2020
payload.core_explanation_md:
- **FCA**: the buyer can instruct its carrier to issue a **bill of lading with an on-board notation** to the seller, so the seller can present it to its bank for **financing**.
- **Own transport**: FCA, DAP, DPU and DDP let buyer or seller use **its own vehicles**, not only a third-party carrier.
- **CIP**: insurance by default is now **Institute Cargo Clauses (A)**, **all risks**, in place of the old limited cover (Clauses C).
- **DPU** replaces **DAT**, and is the **only rule under which the seller unloads** at destination.
- **Costs** tied to carrier charges are set out more clearly.
- **Security** obligations (for example **screening of containers**) are addressed.

Check each term's year in a credit or contract: parties may agree to use an earlier edition if they name it.

payload.title: Case file 1: the credit does not care about the contract
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Scenario.** An importer opens a credit for machinery. The invoice matches the credit, but the importer then says the goods are not what the sales contract promised, and asks the bank to refuse payment.

**Answer.** The bank deals in **documents, not goods**, and the credit is **separate from the sale contract**. If the documents **comply**, the issuing bank must **honour** them. A dispute over the contract is for the buyer and seller, not a reason for the bank to refuse.

Two further points the courseware draws out:
- A **court order** may stop the bank paying, and the bank must then wait; **recovering** money from the applicant is a separate matter of **credit risk**, and should not be linked to honouring the credit.
- A bank must not itself **excuse a payment** by pointing to quality or contract disputes.

payload.title: Case file 2: dates, partial shipments and insurance
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Dates on documents.** A document may be **dated before the credit** was issued, as long as it is **not dated after the expiry date for presentation**, unless the credit says otherwise. The bank should not reject a document merely for pre-dating the credit.

**Partial shipment.** If the credit forbids it, but the goods go on **one vessel on one voyage** under **two bills of lading** with different dates, that is **not** a partial shipment. More than one set of transport documents for the **same means of transport and journey** is not partial even with different dates.

**Insurance.** If the credit is silent, cover must be **at least 110%** of the invoice value. The policy must not be dated **after the transport document**, **unless** it shows cover **from the date of shipment**.

payload.title: Case file 3: the refusal clock, banking days and the closed-bank rule
payload.core_explanation_md:
**Refusal clock.** The issuing bank must give notice of refusal and the discrepancies by the **close of the fifth banking day after the day it received the documents**. **Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays are not banking days**, so a refusal sent on the next working Monday after a weekend may still be on time.

**Closed-bank rule.** If the **last day for presentation** falls on a day the bank is **closed**, it is extended to the **next banking day**. If banks in that place are **open** that day, there is **no extension**.

**Advising failure.** If an advising bank cannot advise a credit, it must tell the issuing bank **at once**. The issuing bank is **not responsible** for the advising bank's failure, even though it chose that bank.

payload.title: Counting five banking days with a holiday
payload.core_explanation_md: Illustrative case: an issuing bank receives documents on Wednesday 8 April 2026. Friday 10 April 2026 is a bank holiday in its city. Saturdays and Sundays are not banking days. By what date must it send notice of refusal?

worked_steps.description: Day 1 is the first banking day after receipt: Thursday 9 April.
Friday 10 April is a holiday and the weekend follows. Day 2 is Monday 13 April.
Days 3, 4 and 5 are Tuesday 14, Wednesday 15 and Thursday 16 April.

payload.final_answer_with_unit: Notice of refusal must go out by the close of Thursday 16 April 2026

self_check.prompt_text: Without the holiday on 10 April, what would the deadline have been?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Wednesday 15 April 2026: Thursday 9, Friday 10, Monday 13, Tuesday 14 and Wednesday 15 are the five banking days.

items.stem_md: Which Incoterms 2020 rule requires the seller to unload the goods from the arriving means of transport at the named destination?

options.text_md: FOB
